header:
Date: 2026-05-07 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Redwood: Maya Chen (AE), Rafael Ortiz (SE)
Greystone: Anika Patel (CTO), Tom Reynolds (ML Eng), Sarah Liao (FinOps), Mark Wu (Procurement)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE, and with me is Rafael, our solutions engineer, we'll run through the console focusing on per-route usage and cost.
[00:14] Anika Patel: Hi, thanks - quick context, we're evaluating inference economics across web and internal routes, and we care a lot about attribution and finite budgets, so excited to see the console.
[00:25] Rafael Ortiz: Great, I'll share my screen in a sec - uh - just so you know the flow, we'll show the high-level usage lens, then drill into specific routes, model mappings, and cost breakdowns.
[00:40] Tom Reynolds: Sounds good, one ask up front - can we see token distributions and avg seq length per route? that's the main thing for our optimizer.
[00:49] Rafael Ortiz: Absolutely, that's exactly where the Optimize recommendations come from - we look at median and 95th percentile seq lengths, batching headroom, cache hit rates.
[01:05] [sfx: screen shared] Rafael Ortiz: Ok jumping into the Console, this is the Usage Overview, top-left you have aggregate tokens and requests, top-right latency heatmap, you can filter by route or model variant.
[01:20] Sarah Liao: Quick clarification, when you say route, is that our internal route id or path - how do you map our app routes to the console?
[01:29] Maya Chen: Good question, you can send a route tag with each request, or we auto-map based on host+path heuristics; for the POC we recommend explicit tags so attribution is exact.
[01:41] Rafael Ortiz: Here is a sample per-route panel, you can see 'web-search' and 'assistant-internal' as separate lines, cost is broken out by model, by token class, and by time window. Notice the small spikes correlate with cached prefix misses.
[01:58] Tom Reynolds: I see a 'cost per 1k tokens' column - is that normalized across quantized variants or is it per selected model artifact?
[02:08] Rafael Ortiz: It's per model variant; the system normalizes to token counts but keeps model-specific throughput and GPU unit costs in the calc. For quantized variants we show adjusted per-token costs and expected latency impact.
[02:23] Anika Patel: Is the KV cache the same as the prefix cache we use in our transformer stack? sometimes vendors talk about cache but mean different things.
[02:33] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, our KV cache refers to attention key/value cache across sequence positions; we also expose 'prefix cache' hits if you're persisting conversation state. UX shows cache hit ratio per route.
[02:44] Sarah Liao: Regarding cost, can we see amortized infra overheads - like reserved GPU cost, storage costs, telemetry overhead?
[02:53] Maya Chen: We provide two views: direct inference cost (model runtime + GPU seconds) and full stack cost that includes reserved capacity amortization, storage for KV, and telemetry sampling. You can toggle to see both.
[03:08] Rafael Ortiz: And there's a Cost Attribution view where you can map costs to business tags - customer, product line, feature flag - and export for your FinOps toolchain.
[03:21] Mark Wu: From procurement we need SLAs and some security bullet points - SOC2, SSO, where logs land.
[03:29] Maya Chen: We'll share our SOC2 and ISO summaries; we support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs to your preferred SIEM, and KMS integration for key management. Link to security pack in notes.
[03:43] Tom Reynolds: Back to performance, can we simulate QPS at scale and see what the console predicts for latency and cost?
[03:50] Rafael Ortiz: Yep we have a benchmark mode - you can upload a traffic profile (we can help synthesize) and the console will estimate 95th latency and projected spend across hosted vs dedicated. That's what we'll run in the POC.
[04:06] [00:04:06] Rafael Ortiz: showing the Optimize panel now - it surfaces batching, cache TTL, and recommended quantization per route. There's a one-click apply for suggested batching windows but we always recommend testing in canary first.
[04:22] Anika Patel: What's the typical uplift on cost we might see from following Optimize suggestions?
[04:28] Rafael Ortiz: In our benchmarks customers see 20-60% per-token cost reduction depending on workload shape; if you have long prefixes and good cache locality you can get bigger wins due to reduced compute.
[04:40] Tom Reynolds: Are there tradeoffs on accuracy from quantization? we need to keep assistant latency but not degrade intent recognition.
[04:48] Rafael Ortiz: Yes quantization can introduce small regressions; the Console ties into Eval results so you can see metric deltas on your validation prompts before rollout. We support canary and A/B on model variants.
[05:02] Sarah Liao: For billing, how granular are invoices - per route, per model, or consolidated?
[05:09] Maya Chen: Invoices are consolidated but we provide per-route breakout CSVs you can import to internal billing. For Dedicated customers we can provide reserved capacity amortization lines.
[05:20] Mark Wu: For the POC, what's the minimum commitment?
[05:25] Maya Chen: For a short POC we typically run a 2-week pilot on Hosted with demo credits and optional Dedicated sizing if you need strict isolation - procurement usually signs a trial addendum. We'll send the details.
[05:36] Rafael Ortiz: Quick demo note - here's a 'cost alert' rule, you can trigger when spend per route exceeds X or when 95th latency breaches SLO; alerts can call webhooks or notify Slack.
[05:49] Anika Patel: Nice. Can we also map user IDs to route spend for customer-level chargebacks?
[05:56] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, if you pass user_id as a tag we can attribute at that granularity, subject to your privacy constraints.
[06:08] Tom Reynolds: About private deployment - we have some PII routes; is Redwood Private an on-prem option?
[06:15] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private runs in your VPC or on-prem, we offer a control plane with customer-managed networking, and HSM/KMS integrations. The console UI is the same in private mode.
[06:29] Sarah Liao: Any hidden costs around telemetry retention or logs export?
[06:35] Rafael Ortiz: We have tiered retention; basic telemetry included, extended retention is an add-on. Logs export to S3 or your SIEM may incur storage egress depending on your infra.
[06:47] Anika Patel: Ok let's talk next steps - we want the benchmark and a pricing estimate for 3 models across two routes.
[06:54] Maya Chen: Great. Rafael will own the benchmark, I'll send pricing. We'll also share SOC2 and the POC addendum. Links: deck https://redwood.ai/decks/greystone-route-econ and bench sheet https://tiny.red/greystone-bench.
[07:08] Mark Wu: Procurement note - we'll need a sample SOW and PO template to speed approvals.
[07:13] Maya Chen: We'll include a sample SOW.
[07:17] Tom Reynolds: Small nit - earlier you mentioned KV cache misses causing spikes, can we get a per-request trace to diagnose?
[07:24] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, the tracing hooks in the Console let you pull a request-level trace including cache hit/miss, model variant chosen, and kernel select. We'll add that to the POC runbook.
[07:36] Anika Patel: That sounds good. I'm comfortable to move forward with a POC contingent on the benchmark meeting our latency SLOs.
[07:44] Maya Chen: Understood. Rafael, anything else to demo?
[07:48] Rafael Ortiz: One last thing - route grouping and tagging; you can create derived routes to roll up microservices cost into product-level metrics. Also the Usage API allows programmatic exports.
[07:59] Sarah Liao: Great, thanks everyone.
[08:02] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifact links and action items.
[08:07] [end]
